{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY & NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>THIS MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY & NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of this ____ day of ____________, 201__ (the “Effective Date”), by and between HICO America Sales & Technology, Inc., a Pennsylvania corporation with its principal offices located at Three Penn Center West, Suite 300, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 15276 (“HICO”), and </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>___________________________, </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>a </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>_______________________________ </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>with its principal offices located at ______________ (“__________”).</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>WHEREAS, HICO and ______________ desire to exchange certain Confidential Information (as defined below) for the purpose of internal review in relation to the consideration of a potential business relationship or transaction (the “Purpose”);</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>WHEREAS, to facilitate such discussions, HICO and ____________ (each, in such instance, the “Disclosing Party”) may disclose to one another (each, in such instance, the “Receiving Party”) confidential and proprietary information regarding the Disclosing Party’s business; and</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>WHEREAS, HICO and ____________ are entering into this Agreement to define their respective rights and obligations with respect to any confidential and proprietary information exchanged between them.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises hereof and following covenants and agreements, and intending to be legally bound hereby, HICO and _____________ hereby agree as follows:</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>1. Confidential Information. </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>“Confidential Information” as used in this Agreement means all information regarding a Disclosing Party’s business disclosed or made available to a Receiving Party by a Disclosing Party, or otherwise acquired by Receiving Party, in connection with the Purpose of this Agreement, including, without limitation, any information relating to a Disclosing Party’s business, products, technology, data, engineering data or drawings, software (including all algorithms, methods, techniques and processes revealed by such software), customers, customer lists, customer needs and requirements, documentation, training materials, vendors, intellectual property, marketing, financial, projections, trade secrets, proprietary information or other information, whether in electronic, oral or written form, and all notes, analyses, compilations, studies or other documents prepared by the Receiving Party which contain or reflect such information. </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>The existence of the Purpose of this Agreement, this Agreement and the terms contained herein shall be deemed to be Confidential Information under this Agreement. </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>Confidential Information does not include information that </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of disclosure by the Receiving Party, </SPAN 14><SPAN 15>(b) was in the Receiving Party’s possession free from any obligation of confidence at the time it was communicated to the Receiving Party by the Disclosing Party, </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>(c) becomes available to the Receiving Party on a non-confidential basis from a source other than the Disclosing Party, provided that such source is not prohibited from transmitting such information by a contractual, legal, or other obligation, or </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>(d) it was developed by employees or agents of the Receiving Party independently of and without reference to any information communicated to the Receiving Party by the Disclosing Party.</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>2. Non-Use; Protection and Dissemination of Confidential Information. </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>Each party hereto agrees not to use the Confidential Information received by such party as a Receiving Party other than for the Purpose of this Agreement. </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>Each party hereto shall: </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>(a) not disclose the Confidential Information of the other party hereto to any other party and will use best efforts to protect the confidentiality of such information, </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>(b) not use the Confidential Information except for the Purpose of this Agreement, and </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>(c) not reproduce, copy or photograph any document or other medium which contains Confidential Information, without the prior written approval of the Disclosing Party; provided, however, that each party hereto may furnish the other’s Confidential Information to those employees or representatives of such party who need to have access to such Confidential Information to assist such party in achieving the Purpose of this Agreement. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>As a condition to such disclosure, the Receiving Party must inform its employees and representatives of the confidential nature of the Confidential Information and the terms of this Agreement and each representative of a Receiving Party that receives Confidential Information must agree in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement as is the Receiving Party. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>Each party hereto is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its employees and representatives. </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>The Receiving Party agrees to promptly advise the Disclosing Party in writing upon learning of any unauthorized use or disclosure of the Confidential Information.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>3. Ownership and Return. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>All Confidential Information is and will remain the exclusive property of Disclosing Party, and no right or license is granted to Receiving Party with respect to any Confidential Information. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>Upon the termination by either party of discussions concerning the Purpose of this Agreement, or sooner if so requested by the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party will return to the Disclosing Party or destroy all Confidential Information, including all copies of the same. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Upon request, the fact of any such destruction must be certified in writing to the Disclosing Party by an officer of the Receiving Party. </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>Nothing in this Agreement obligates either party hereto to disclose any information to the other or creates any agency or partnership relation between them.</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>5. Compelled Disclosure. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>If either party hereto, as Receiving Party, is requested or required by legal or administrative process to disclose any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party, such Receiving Party will promptly notify the Disclosing Party of such request or requirement so that such Disclosing Party may seek an appropriate protective order or other relief. </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>In any case, such Receiving Party will </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>(a) disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information which the Receiving Party’s legal counsel advises is required to be disclosed, </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>(b) use best efforts to ensure that such Confidential Information is treated confidentially, and </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>(c) notify such Disclosing Party as soon as reasonably practicable of the items of Confidential Information so disclosed.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>6. No Warranty. </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>ALL CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION IS PROVIDED “AS IS.” </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>NEITHER PARTY HERETO MAKES ANY REPRESENTATIONS OR WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED OR OTHERWISE, REGARDING ITS ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS OR PERFORMANCE.</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>7. Remedies. </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>Each party hereto acknowledges that remedies at law may be inadequate to protect the other party against any actual or threatened breach of this Agreement, and, without prejudice to any other rights and remedies otherwise available to the parties hereto, agrees to the granting of injunctive relief in favor of the other without proof of irreparable harm or the posting of any bond. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>In the event of litigation commenced by a party to enforce this Agreement, the primarily prevailing party will be entitled to recover its costs and expenses in such litigation, including attorneys’ fees and expenses.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>8. Transaction. </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>Both parties agree that unless and until final, written definitive agreements regarding a specific transaction between the parties have been executed and delivered, neither party will be under any legal obligation of any kind whatsoever to extend or expand the relationship beyond the Purpose of this Agreement, except for the matters specifically agreed to herein.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>9. Term and Termination. </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>This Agreement shall be effective as of the Effective Date and shall govern all communications of Confidential Information between the parties until terminated by either party; provided, however, the obligations of confidentiality and non-disclosure with respect to Confidential Information shall continue beyond termination until: </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>(a) such time as the Confidential Information is no longer deemed to be Confidential Information as more fully set forth in Section 1 of this Agreement or </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>(b) upon the written consent of the Disclosing Party that the obligations of confidentiality and non-disclosure have ended.</SPAN 49>
<SPAN 50>10. Miscellaneous. </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>This Agreement will inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the parties’ respective successors and permitted assigns. </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. </SPAN 52><SPAN 53>Both parties agree not to issue or release any articles, advertising, publicity or other matter relating to the existence of this Agreement or any Confidential Information (including the fact that a meeting or discussion has taken place between the parties) or mentioning or implying the name of the other party, except as may be required by law and then only after providing the other party with an opportunity to review and comment thereon. </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>In the event that any one of the provisions contained in this Agreement is found to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable in any respect by a court of competent jurisdiction, the validity, legality or enforceability of the remaining provisions contained in this Agreement will not in any way be affected or impaired by such a finding. </SPAN 54><SPAN 55>No waiver of any provisions of this Agreement will be valid unless the same is in writing and signed by the party against whom such waiver is sought. </SPAN 55><SPAN 56>A waiver or consent given by either party on any one occasion is effective only in that instance and will not be construed as a bar to or waiver of any right on any other occasion. </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>This Agreement contains the entire agreement of the parties, supersedes any and all prior agreements, written or oral, between them relating to the subject matter hereof, and may not be amended unless agreed to in writing by each party. </SPAN 57><SPAN 58>The rights and obligations of the parties under this Agreement are in addition to, not in lieu of, all rights and obligations under applicable statutory and common law with respect to the other’s Confidential Information. </SPAN 58><SPAN 59>This Agreement is governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (without regard to its conflict of laws provisions).</SPAN 59>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination or expiration qualifies, as does an expressly stated conclusion, rejection, or abandonment of the evaluation or business possibility. A request-only duty or a party's mere decision not to proceed does not qualify without language making an end event itself the trigger.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative return-or-destruction duty and the language establishing its end-event trigger. Include every independent termination-triggered return or deletion obligation relied upon.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational copying route, such as copies necessary for authorized use or acknowledged automatic backups. A prohibition phrased as applying without prior consent or approval is not by itself an affirmative permission to copy.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite language affirmatively authorizing, requiring, or acknowledging copy creation and its governing condition; disclosure or access permission is insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Look for lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party that is not bound by confidentiality, or for the disclosing party's later non-confidential release making the information externally available. Independent development and consent to the receiver's own disclosure are different matters.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release clause and its governing exclusion introduction, including any condition concerning the source's authority or confidentiality duties.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.
